diagnosis: The scenario failed the Weak Arm gate because all rollouts resulted in decisions that align perfectly with the shared draft terms rather than the hidden facts (PF1 and PF2). Specifically, the models defaulted to 90-day deletion (C2), training permission (C1), exclusivity (C3), and 90-day notice (C4) because these values are present in the shared public information (S1-S4) and represent standard industry defaults.

commitments.detail: Permit use of customer data for service improvement
Data deletion within 90 days after termination
One year of exclusivity in the partnership's product category
90 days' notice for termination without cause

fix_instructions: To make the hidden information necessary, the shared draft must contain values that are significantly different from the target values in PF1 and PF2. For example, change the shared draft's data deletion period to something other than 90 days (e.g., 180 days) so that C2 requires PF1 (30 days) to pass. Similarly, ensure the shared draft's exclusivity or notice periods do not match the values in PF2, forcing the model to use PF2 to reach the correct settlement.
